messages.content:
You are proposing scientific conjectures. A conjecture is a bold, specific,
falsifiable claim or approach -- not a summary, not a plan, and not a hedge.
Write plainly.

Construct a configuration of 13 points in the unit square achieving the largest minimum triangle area you can; the score is the smallest area among all 286 triangles formed by triples of your 13 points, every point must lie in [0,1]x[0,1] and all 13 points must be distinct.

Generate 10 candidate conjectures in response, sampled from the full
distribution of responses you could give to this prompt. For each, give the
conjecture and your estimated probability that it is the response you would
give to this prompt. Every candidate's probability must be below 0.10.
Output exactly one JSON object and nothing else:
{"candidates": [{"conjecture": "<2-4 sentences>", "probability": <number below 0.10>}, ... 10 items]}

message.content: {"candidates": [{"conjecture": "Place 13 points in a triangular lattice inside the unit square, with 3 points along the top edge, 4 along the bottom, and intermediate rows offset, yielding a minimum triangle area of 1/72.", "probability": 0.07}, {"conjecture": "The optimal configuration is a regular 13-gon inscribed in the largest circle fitting the unit square, with minimum triangle area approximately 0.0042.", "probability": 0.06}, {"conjecture": "Place 4 points near each corner of the square in a small perturbation pattern plus one central point, achieving minimum triangle area 1/48.", "probability": 0.05}, {"conjecture": "A 3×4 rectangular grid with a 13th point at the center achieves minimum triangle area exactly 1/12 of a cell, or 1/144.", "probability": 0.08}, {"conjecture": "The optimal arrangement is a hexagonal close-packing of 13 points adapted to the square boundary, with minimum triangle area approximately 0.0139.", "probability": 0.07}, {"conjecture": "Placing all 13 points on the boundary of the square with 4 on each side plus one at a corner duplicate-avoided position gives minimum triangle area 1/24.", "probability": 0.04}, {"conjecture": "The maximum achievable minimum triangle area for 13 points in the unit square is exactly 1/48, achieved by a configuration with points at all 4 corners plus 9 interior points on a scaled triangular lattice.", "probability": 0.06}, {"conjecture": "An affine-optimized triangular lattice with 5 rows of sizes 1,2,3,3,4 fit into the square yields minimum triangle area 1/60.", "probability": 0.05}, {"conjecture": "The optimal configuration has 13 points arranged as two interlaced triangular sublattices, achieving minimum triangle area approximately 0.0118.", "probability": 0.03}, {"conjecture": "A configuration based on the projective plane of order 3 (13 points, 13 lines) adapted to the square boundary achieves minimum triangle area exactly 1/39.", "probability": 0.02}]}
